John shared a university degree-completion certificate and said he graduated in late March 2023. He values turning words into action and finds helping others rewarding. Maria offered support; they recalled volunteering together the prior year. Photos showed a man and woman shaking hands over a food tray and a woman/child walking in a park.

The instructor ensures proper poses, encourages listening to the body, and creates a relaxed, welcoming environment. A photo showed a man doing yoga outdoors on a blue mat. Maria participated the previous weekend in a 5K charity run for a homeless shelter, enjoying the unity and energy; she shared a large group walking down a street. John volunteered at a career fair at a local school and saw how lack of resources affects children’s dreams; he shared a heart-shaped sign reading **“Always look on the bright side of life.”** He pledged to keep supporting children’s dreams. Both reaffirmed that community members can make a difference.
- **10 Apr 2023 (Session 11, 6:13 p.m.):** John said his car broke down on **Friday, 7 Apr 2023**, while he was going to work. He shared a photo of a mountain with a sunset and flowers in the foreground, reminding him of a road trip they took the previous year. He and Maria said they explored the Pacific Northwest coast and visited national parks; the beauty gave perspective, peace, hope, power, and inspiration during hard times. She bought a cross necklace to feel closer to her faith and said shelter residents have become like family; she feels blessed to know them. She shared a photo of people around a food-filled table from a meal organized for shelter residents, where she helped prepare everything. The gathering created comfort, community, and mutual support. They reaffirmed that kindness, relationships, and community make a real difference. John thanked her for being a positive force and told her to stay safe.

rebuild.11:
- John and Maria are close friends, “great teammates,” and committed to supporting each other, serving others, and improving their community. They value kindness, compassion, optimism, nature, peace, hope, relationships, and community.

- John returned from a fun family road trip on December 16, 2022. In 2022, he and Maria also traveled along the Pacific Northwest coast and visited several national parks; John found the scenery breathtaking. John practices kickboxing, which gives him energy, and planned to practice taekwondo on December 22, 2022. Maria keeps fit and recently began aerial yoga.

- John hopes to enter or run for local political office. His main priorities are education and infrastructure, inspired by seeing his neighborhood suffer from underfunded schools and crumbling infrastructure while growing up. He believes schools and infrastructure should be properly funded so future generations have better opportunities. He researches local politics, talks with leaders and organizations, gathers ideas and support, and wants to turn words into practical solutions. Community meetings and conversations have deepened his understanding of local problems. He has repeatedly advocated more school funding, resources, supplies, and equipment, especially for children facing inequality.

- John first campaigned before February 2023 and described it as a wild ride; he decided to run again because it showed him the positive impact he could make. He is also considering policymaking after completing a university degree during March 26–April 1, 2023. He is especially interested in education and infrastructure. He wants to serve his country and community and feels supported and proud of that goal.

- In 2021, John shared a photo of men repairing a school after funding enabled needed renovations, making it safer and more modern. He attended a community meeting on January 28, 2023, where local concerns and upgrades were discussed; he was upset by the state of education and heartbroken that some children lacked supplies. Maria agreed that education benefits everyone and suggested pursuing money/resources and raising awareness. John has children who have many resources and wants to address the inequality affecting other children.

- John organized a food drive for neighbors who lost jobs, motivated by unemployment in his community. It received an overwhelming response with many volunteers. Maria offered to help with networking and future drives. John and Maria also volunteered together during 2022 and agreed on April 2, 2023, to keep improving other people’s lives.

- John joined a service-focused online group during December 25–31, 2022. The emotional experience gave him connection, purpose, new perspectives, inspiring stories, advice, and encouragement. The group distributed food and supplies at a homeless shelter, organized a toy drive, and brainstormed projects involving education, mentorship, job training, and résumé building for underserved people.

- John failed a military aptitude test shortly before January 1, 2023, and felt stressed, but retook it during February 27–March 5 and received results he considered great. Maria supported him. John discussed serving his country with family and friends, who supported his motivation. A photo showed a wooden sign with a flag and eagle.

- John had an unexpected travel incident during January 2–8, 2023; a photo showed a car with a broken windshield. He stayed calm, sought assistance, returned home safely, and felt relieved and grateful. Maria shared a tattoo quote as a reminder to stay strong. John uses sunsets to calm down and remember life’s small joys. Maria’s December 2022 beach sunset photo (ocean, wave, sunset) reminded him of a childhood film camera and beach photos. Maria finds sunsets peaceful and connecting to nature.

- John’s family is his “rock,” giving him strength, love, focus, and motivation. On December 22, 2022, he shared family picnic, playground swing, and dinner photos. They enjoy climbing, sliding, games, cooking pizza with varied toppings, laughter, and shared meals. John regularly takes his children to parks; on March 4–5, 2023, everyone swung at the park. He chooses walks, picnics, local events, and other activities to make memories. His family enjoyed a violin concert during February 27–March 5. John’s son Kyle was one year old on March 6, 2023; John describes parenting as difficult but overwhelmingly loving and happy.

- Maria’s family is small. She enjoys movies, hiking, and game nights with friends and values quality connections. As a child she enjoyed activities with siblings. She made a castle shadow box and castle painting after a trip to England, including London, whose architecture and history captivated her; the artwork brings the beauty and magic of castles/London into her home.

- Maria volunteers at a homeless shelter, began volunteering because of her aunt’s example and help during Maria’s family’s financial hardship, and feels happy when brightening someone’s day. She formed trust with shelter residents through listening and compassion and considers them like family. On January 21, 2023, during a children’s event, she comforted an approximately eight-year-old girl who had no other family; they eventually laughed together. Maria organized/prepared a shelter meal shortly before April 10, 2023, creating warmth, comfort, and community. She also gave fulfilling talks there and received compliments. A cross necklace bought to feel closer to her faith made her happy.

- Maria participated in a charity event on January 27, 2023, serving meals; she found recipients’ gratitude heartwarming. She met David, whose hardship humbled her, and connected him with an organization providing housing/support for homeless people. She ran a homeless-shelter 5K on April 1–2, 2023, enjoying the unity, energy, and shared charitable purpose.

- On February 24, 2023, Maria met Jean at the shelter. Jean had experienced divorce, job loss, and homelessness but remained optimistic, grateful, resilient, and convinced in kindness. Maria and John found Jean inspiring and agreed that kindness, positivity, gratitude, and hope can produce joy despite hardship. Maria took a poetry class as of April 2, 2023, to express feelings; it was difficult but beneficial. She had also taken an enlightening creative-writing class by February 25.

- Maria’s grandmother died during February 27–March 5, 2023; on March 6 she was grieving while trying to stay positive. John offered support and shared a family picnic photo. Maria believes nature and small joys help people through difficult times.

- John volunteered at a local school career fair on April 1–2, 2023, saw how limited resources affect children’s dreams, and found helping them rewarding. A sign read “Always look on the bright side of life.” He intends to keep advocating for children and believes communities must work together.

- John began a weekend beginner yoga class with colleague Rob on April 7, 2023. It teaches poses, stretching, and breathing; yoga is now part of his daily routine and improves relaxation, flexibility, mindfulness, mental/physical well-being, and peace of mind. He praises the instructor’s careful guidance and welcoming atmosphere. A photo showed a man practicing outdoors on a blue mat.

- John’s car broke down while going to work on Friday, April 7, 2023. Repairs were difficult and strained his finances, but he remained positive and sought solutions. A mountain/sunset/flowers photo reminded him of his and Maria’s 2022 road trip.
